w:r.w:t: shows how the payment adapter sits between ACME and the gateway.
The checkout service never handles raw card numbers: card data is tokenised in the browser by the PayFlow SDK, and only tokens reach ACME systems.
: receives orders from the web shop and owns the order state.
: translates domain commands into PayFlow API calls. It is the only component holding gateway credentials.
Gateway errors are mapped to adapter behaviour in the appendix (
The adapter shall send amounts in minor currency units.
Every authorisation request shall carry an idempotency key.
The adapter should time out after 10 s and retry at most twice, reusing the idempotency key.
Partial refunds shall be supported up to the captured amount.
Refunds older than 180 days are rejected by PayFlow and must be handled manually by Finance.
Events are signed with HMAC-SHA256. The receiver verifies the signature before parsing the body (
def verify(payload: bytes, header: str, secret: bytes) -> bool:
The receiver shall reject events whose signature does not verify, and log them.
PayFlow’s sandbox can replay any event from its dashboard, which makes signature failures easy to reproduce.
